Over half of the beneficiaries of UNDP's energy portfolio are in countries in crisis settings. So what have we learned?
 
🔸First, that digital tools are changing how we can scale resilient energy systems. Geospatial mapping, digital twins, and AI-based risk models are transforming how we can mitigate vulnerability.
 
🔹Second, that energy is foundational infrastructure for recovery. An investment in energy infrastructure is an investment in rebuilding water services, health, communications, and livelihoods.
 
♦️Third, that in fragile contexts, energy finance is beyond risk mitigation; it’s about making resilience bankable. Less than 0.5% of global adaptation finance reaches energy systems. Countries are leveraging mechanisms like parametric insurance and regional risk pools to bring multiples on returns in investment.
 
These efforts are already accelerating - from solarizing hospitals and clinics in Yemen, to restoring decentralized power in Ukraine, to bringing renewable energy to crisis-affected communities across Sudan, Somalia, and the Sahel. Read more in our new Sustainable Energy Bulletin on Crisis Settings 👉 https://lnkd.in/eBAMvFDe
